checks.item: 1821: Independence: the Trigarante Army enters. The Army of the Three Guarantees enters Mexico City on 27 September 1821, ending Spanish rule.
checks.found: History of Mexico City: image caption 'Entry of the Three Guarantees Army into Mexico City on September 27, 1821', but the body text says the army 'entered Mexico City on 21 September 1821' with independence declared 'on the following 27 September'. Army of the Three Guarantees: 'On September 27, 1821, the Army of the Three Guarantees triumphantly entered Mexico City, led by Iturbide.'
checks.detail: 27 September 1821 is supported by the cited page's caption and by the army's own article; the '21 September' in the cited page's body text is an inconsistency in that page, so the data was left as it is.

checks.item: 2016: Federal District renamed Ciudad de México. On 29 January 2016 the Federal District officially becomes Ciudad de México (CDMX), with greater autonomy.
checks.found: 'On 29 January 2016, the Federal District was officially renamed Ciudad de México, or CDMX. These reforms granted the city greater autonomy'.

summary: All 10 sampled items matched their cited sources and nothing was changed. One caution on the 1821 milestone: the cited History of Mexico City article is internally inconsistent about the entry date (body text 21 September, image caption 27 September); the stored 27 September agrees with the Army of the Three Guarantees article.
